mechanism_narrative: The four-week decline in WORKPLACES from -17.9 to -50.1 removes commuting trips that anchor weekday retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC continues lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES falls from -17.9 at t-3w to -50.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES continues to decline or stays below -50.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls below -35 percent of baseline, reduced station activity signifies enforced travel limits that suppress non-essential retail trips, driving RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -35 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT is below -35, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is not lower than the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A joint pattern of falling WORKPLACES and rising RESIDENTIAL indicates home-centered routines; when both occur, retail-and-recreation trips are substituted by at-home activity, lowering RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days when WORKPLACES is below -30 and RESIDENTIAL is above 2.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, the PARKS surge to 65.1 reflects outdoor recreation substituting for indoor commercial leisure, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds 60 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rises from 43.4 at t-3w to 65.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: When PARKS exceeds 60, RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is higher than the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained PARKS readings above 40 mark favorable spring weather that increases overall out-of-home activity, spilling over into nearby retail-and-recreation visits and lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remains above 42 for all four snapshot weeks
failure_condition: With PARKS above 40, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The drop in GROCERY_PHARM from 5.4 to -11.6 signals reduced essential errands; because retail-and-recreation trips are partly bundled with grocery trips, RETAIL_REC falls further over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM falls from 5.3 at t-2w to -11.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM is below 0, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not lower than the prior 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of TRANSIT below -30 and WORKPLACES below -45 reflects a broad reduction in permitted out-of-home activity; this policy-induced contraction lowers RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days when TRANSIT is below -30 and WORKPLACES is below -45.

mechanism_narrative: A rising RESIDENTIAL share with high PARKS indicates local neighborhood activity; if residential stays above 2 and parks above 50, nearby retail benefits from hyperlocal footfall, lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than the prior 14 days when RESIDENTIAL is above 2 and PARKS is above 50.
